title: Swap a Vec of JoinHandle for a JoinSet
summary: Handles awaited front to back become a JoinSet read in completion order with abort_all, and a panicked JoinError is traced back to its file.

turns.user: import_all waits for everything before it errors, even when one file is just missing. if the first one is heavy that's like a minute. and after it returns the error the other tasks keep running

assistant.body: TL;DR: the JoinHandles sit in a Vec and are awaited front to back. If the third one fails at once, you still cannot see its Err until the first one finishes. Dropping a JoinHandle does not stop its task either, so the rest keep running after ? returns. Spawn into a JoinSet instead, take results with join_next in the order they finish, and call abort_all on the first failure. A panic inside a task also comes back through ? as a JoinError, so the process stays up and with_context still tells you which file it was.

turns.user: one broken CSV made parse_row panic and the error is just `task 14 panicked with message "row without a comma"`. which file??

assistant.body: Apologies, I checked again and that was not accurate. with_context only applies when import_file returns an Err. A panic unwinds the task before that point, so the JoinError holds nothing but the task Id. Keep the id() of the AbortHandle that spawn returns in a HashMap next to its path, and receive with join_next_with_id. On a panic, JoinError::id() finds the owner and its path goes on as context.

turns.user: actually a panic is a bug, don't turn it into an error, just crash. log which file though

assistant.body: Sure. JoinError::into_panic takes out the panic payload and std::panic::resume_unwind throws it on to the caller. The path is printed with eprintln before unwinding. Note: into_panic panics itself on a cancelled JoinError, but this function only calls abort_all right before it returns, so what arrives here is always a panic.
